messages:
customer-jw: Hey team — since last night our private Redwood inference endpoint in us-west-2 intermittently fails for probes > 1s. App logs show TLS handshake errors and sporadic connection resets. Request id=req-7f3a. We're behind a NAT + custom NACL/SG. Any quick checks?

jenna: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick Qs: are failures 100% or intermittent? Do you see 4xx/5xx from the control plane or just connection-level errors? Can you paste a curl/openssl trace and your NACL/SG egress rules?

customer-jw: Intermittent, ~30% of requests fail during bursts. App shows: "error: handshake failure: EOF" and occasional "connect: connection reset by peer". Control plane logs show timeouts, not 4xx. Here's trimmed tcpdump around a failed connection:

    12:04:11.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 52.34.120.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
    12:04:11.223456 IP 52.34.120.45.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0

(Not consistent for every failure). NACL outbound rules: allow 0.0.0.0/0 443, deny 0.0.0.0/0 tcp 32768-65535 (rule 100), allow ephemeral 49152-65535 (rule 200). SG outbound all traffic allowed.

sam: That NACL setup looks suspicious. Remember NACLs are stateless — you need explicit allow for both directions using the ephemeral port ranges your OS uses. Also NACL entries are evaluated by rule number (lowest first). If rule 100 is deny for 32768-65535 and appears before the allow for 49152-65535, you can get gaps depending on client ephemeral range. Which OS / ephemeral range are you using?

customer-jw: We're on Amazon Linux 2; default ephemeral is 32768-60999 in our images. I copied the NACL from an older template.

rahul: Bingo. Ephemeral range 32768-60999 intersects with that deny. When your client uses an ephemeral port in the denied range, response packets from the Redwood endpoint (dest port = ephemeral) are dropped by NACL and the server sees a reset or handshake fail. That explains intermittent behaviour during bursts.

jenna: Two immediate options: 1) remove the blanket deny rule (100) or reorder so the allow for 32768-65535 is a lower rule number than the deny, or 2) narrow the deny to a smaller set if you need it. Recommended quick fix: add explicit NACL allow entries for both ephemeral egress (32768-65535) and destination 443. Also verify inbound NACL allows the ephemeral response ports.

sam: To inspect and patch quickly via CLI (example):

    # describe current NACL entries
    aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0abcd1234

    # add allow for ephemeral range (egress rule number 50)
    aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abcd1234 --rule-number 50 --protocol 6 --port-range From=32768,To=65535 --egress --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --rule-action allow

Replace rule-number with something lower than the deny. Also double-check there isn't a managed firewall on the NAT instance.

customer-jw: Running the describe now. Also our NAT gateway health checks were green. Do I need to touch the SGs?

rahul: SGs are stateful; since outbound is allowed you're fine there. The issue is NACL stateless behavior. Make sure both inbound and outbound NACL entries for ephemeral ranges are allowed.

jenna: If you want to reproduce locally before the change, you can force the client ephemeral port with curl + iptables to bind and then test, or use socat: 

    # example: force source port 33000 from a docker test host\    socat - TCP:52.34.120.45:443,sourceport=33000

That will show whether responses are dropped. Also run tcpdump on the NAT to see the SYN,SYN-ACK sequence.

ingress-bot: Created support incident INC-4892 and attached tcpdump + NACL config. Assigned to eng-sre for postmortem.

sam: After the customer added an allow for 32768-65535 (egress rule 50) and mirrored it on inbound, we saw immediate drop in errors. Monitoring latency and error rate.

customer-jw: Confirmed — error rate down to <1% after rule change. Thanks! We'll keep the change and review security posture with infra.

jenna: Glad that fixed it. Follow-ups: (a) decide if you need a narrower ephemeral allow and adjust client OS ephemeral range (sysctl) to a known subset, (b) document the NACL rule-number ordering and ephemeral ranges in your runbook, (c) we'll liaise with eng-sre to add a KB article.

rahul: Adding note: some OS use 49152-65535, others 32768-60999. Always align NACL entries to the actual endpoints.

customer-jw: Will do. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
